ai.description: The Poona Skink reaches 6 cm in snout-vent length. It is brown with a dark lateral stripe and pale spots. Key features include a transparent palpebral disc and a lack of supranasal scales.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Eurylepis poonaensis* is best distinguished by its distinctively large, shield-like supranasal scales that meet at the midline, separating the rostral from the frontonasal.
ai.habitat: The Poona Skink inhabits the rocky, semi-arid scrublands of the Deccan Plateau, typically found at elevations between 500 and 700 meters.
ai.behavior: The Poona skink is a diurnal, ground-dwelling lizard that actively forages for small insects and invertebrates among leaf litter and rocky crevices during the day.
ai.reproductionNotes: The Poona Skink (*Eurylepis poonaensis*) is oviparous, laying a clutch of 3–5 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, from June to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Eurylepis poonaensis* is endemic to the northern Western Ghats in Maharashtra, India, typically found at elevations between 500 and 1,000 meters.
